correctness.rationale: For the unhalved logarithmic cross ratio, the 4 facet quotients give the exact 12 half-space constraints. Same-axis pairs give J(u)×J(v); at each corner one cross inequality clips an explicit triangle with area T, and all four clips are disjoint by their coordinate-side separation. Summation gives (1). The J(w) length inequality proves unique center optimality; expansion of four T terms yields the exact Hessian. A standalone independent Sutherland–Hodgman clipping and shoelace implementation agreed at 350 seeded center/radius combinations and 150 direct line-boundary cross-ratio comparisons. Numerical checks support, not replace, proof; the geometric decomposition is valid for all interior coordinates and positive finite radii.

value.rationale: The full finite-radius Euclidean mass function is a natural object for uniformly sampling square Hilbert geometry, where arbitrary center positions produce different polygonal ball shapes. The exact closed four-corner profile yields a unique globally maximal center and a strictly negative Hessian of explicitly radius-dependent magnitude. This quantitative all-center stability is not just the known general polygonal construction, a finite sample, or a one-off numerical invariant. It supplies a baseline for Euclidean-volume sampling and comparison with nonsimplicial Hilbert geometries.
